PREFACE 
I, the Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and 
Family Welfare, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, present this 
One Hundred Thirtieth Report of the Committee on Action Taken by Government on the 
Recommendations/ Observations contained in One Hundred Twenty Third Report on the "Outbreak of 
Pandemic Covid-19 and its Management".  
2. The One Hundred Twenty Third Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Health and Family Welfare was presented to the Hon'ble Chairman Rajya Sabha on 21st 
November, 2020 and to both Houses of Parliament on 2 nd February, 2021.  Action  Taken Notes of the 
Government on the recommendations contained in the Report was received from the Ministry on July 20, 
2021.   
3.  The Committee has noted that the statement on the status of implementation of the 
recommendations contained in the said Rep ort of the Committee has not been laid on the Table of Rajya 
Sabha and Lok Sabha in pursuant to the direction of Chairman, Rajya Sabha dated 24th September, 2004 
4.  The Committee made a total of 108 recommendations in its 123 rd Report. Out of the 108  
recommendations, a total number of 52 recommendations accepted by the Ministry has been categorized 
under Chapter -I and there are a total number of 22 recommendations, which the Committee does not 
desire to pursue in view of the Ministry‟s replies, has be en categorized under Chapter-II. A total number 
of 26 recommendations/ observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not been accepted 
by the Committee and the Committee has made further recommendations thereon, has been categorized 
under C hapter-III while a total number of 8 recommendations/observations in respect of which final 
replies of the Ministry have not been received, has been categorized under Chapter-IV. 
5. The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meet ing held on the 1st 
December, 2021.

CHAPTER - I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
ADNIMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF LOCKDOWN & UNLOCKING  
Observation/Recommendation 
1.1 The Committee is of the view that if we had not hit the history books for guidance, the 
reality would have hit us harder. The Government of India learnt from its experience and took 
successful measures like Janta curfew, imposition of 4 months long lockdown and its gradual 
opening, travel restrictions and other social distancing measures to contain the spread of 
Corona virus. The Committee appreciates the measures but also ob serves that there have been 
few glaring lapses in the battle against pandemic like shortage of emergency supplies, red -
tapism, shortage and quality of testing kits, delay in domestic production etc. 
                        (Para 1.42) 
Action Taken 
1.2 Noted. Yes, in the initial phase of the pandemic, there were issues with the indigenous 
capacity in terms of personal protective equipment, N -95 masks, testing kits, ventilators. 
Government of India rose to the occasion and ensured that the local demand fo r the same is met 
through indigenous production as there was global scarcity for all these items.  
1.3 To fast -track informed decision making and to cut down on the procedural delays, 11 
High level Empowered Groups were formed. Based on the evolving needs and scenario in the 
country, on 11th September 2020, these groups were condensed into six larger empowered 
groups (EGs). Four of the EGs are headed by the departmental secretaries and one each by NITI 
Aayog officials. Each EG is tasked with respective func tions: (i) medical infrastructure and 
COVID management plan, (ii) ensuring availability of essential medical equipment and 
augmenting human resources., disease surveillance and testing, (iii) coordinating with the private 
sector, NGOs and international org anizations for response -related activities, (iv) economic and 
welfare measures, (v) information, communication, public awareness, public grievances and data 
management, (vi) strategic issues related to COVID management, and facilitating supply chain 
and lo gistics management. On 8 th January 2021, another Empowered Group on Vaccine 
Administration has been constituted to take all necessary measures for effective implementation 
of CO-WIN platform created for inventory management and delivery of COVID-19 vaccine. 
CONTINGENCY PLAN 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.4 The Committee is of the view that the unprecedented outbreak of Corona  virus required a 
well-planned and coordinated response from the Central as well as State Governments for 
successful containment of the pandemic. There must be an integrated as well as a decentralized 
response to outbreak of pandemic Covid -19 for rescuing t he common masses. The disease trend 
data under IDSP is crucial for generating the required response to contain the outbreak 

3 
 
especially when Inter Sectoral Coordination for zoonotic diseases is one of the main programme 
components of IDSP. The Committee is constrained to observe the failure of National Centre for 
Disease Control -Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (NCDC -IDSP) in generating the 
required response in the wake of the pandemic. The Committee feels that NCDP -IDSP should 
have been utilized in  a more effective manner especially when the sole objective of IDSP is to 
detect and respond to outbreaks in the early rising phase through trained Rapid Response Teams 
(RRTs). The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends for revitalizing the enshrined ro le and 
responsibility of NCDC for effective control of the disease along with strengthening of the 
Central Surveillance Unit (CSU), State Surveillance Units (SSU) and District Surveillance Units 
(DSU). The Committee also recommends the Ministry to effectiv ely implement the various 
programme components under IDSP. The Committee would like the Ministry to launch 
Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme in the remaining States i.e. beyond existing 9 States. 
The Committee observes that there is an urgent need to assess the financial requirement for 
NCDP-IDSP for its revitalization.  
1.5 The Committee, in this connection, strongly recommends the Ministry to chalk out 
strategy and specific course of action to revamp the institutional and Human Resource 
Management structure and further strengthen NCDP -IDSP and pursue with the Ministry of 
Finance for higher budgetary allocation to NCDP-IDSP.  
                                      (Para 2.20) 
Action Taken 
 
1.6 In 2015 Joint Monitoring Mission report of Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme 
(IDSP) recommended review and redesign the IDSP surveillance system, including re -
prioritization of the list of diseases under the IDSP. Subsequently, IDSP, NCDC, re -prioritized 
33 priority health conditions for surveillance. 
1.7 Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) is designed & developed by WHO and 
MoHFW in order to have real time data reported under IDSP and different National Health 
Programmes. It is a web -enabled, near -real-time electronic health information syst em that is 
embedded with all applicable  Government of India's e -Governance standards, Information 
Technology (IT), data &meta data standards to provide state -of-the-art single operating picture 
with geospatial information. 
1.8 IHIP implemented currently in 9 States and has now been expanded to all States in April, 
2021. The IHIP is being aligned with the vision document 2035 and roadmap for public health 
surveillance of NITI Aayog. 
1.9 Under the Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat, the following interventions at an e stimated outlay 
of Rs. 3060 Crores have been made to strengthen NCDC and public health surveillance & 
response: 
 Strengthening of the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), its 5 regional 
branches and 20 metropolitan health surveillance units 
 Setting up integrated public health labs in all districts and 3382 block public health units 
in 11 States 
 Expansion of the Integrated Health Information Portal to all States/UTs to connect all 
public health labs.  

4 
 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.10 The Committee believes that contact tracing, testing and isolating are the crucial 
components for Covid -19 containment strategy. The Committee is of the view that poor contact 
tracing and slow testing in the initial phase of pandemic led to the increased number of 
infections in the country. 
                                      (Para 2.26) 
Action Taken 
 
1.11 Noted. During VC‟s, through formal communications and deployment of multi -
disciplinary Central teams, States have been repeatedly advised to increase efforts on contact 
tracing with the target to track, trace and test 30 contacts per confirmed case to stop the chain of 
disease transmission in the country. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.12 The Committee observes that the Pradhan Mantri Atma Nirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana is 
an ambitious program of the government that encompasses vital components to consolidate and 
enrich health infrastructure in the country. The Committee recommends that government should 
not leave any stone unturned in implementing its every component to achieve its cherished goal. 
                                     (Para 2.29) 
Action Taken 
 
1.13 Recommendations of the Committee have been noted. 
 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.14 The Committee observes that the total number of Government hospital beds in the  
country was grossly inadequate keeping in view the rising incidence of Covid-19 cases. Attention 
of the Committee has also been brought to Media Reports which highlighted the abysmally low 
number of beds in Government hospitals in the country especially a t the peak of the pandemic. 
Data from National Health Profile –2019 states that there are total 7,13,986 Government 
hospital beds available in India which amounts to 0.55 beds per 1,000 population. As per 
Reports, 12 States stand below the national level fi gure. The Committee notes that lack of 
hospital beds and the inadequate ventilators further complicated the efficacy of the containment 
plan against the pandemic. As the numbers of cases were on the rise, a frantic search for vacant 
hospital beds became qu ite harrowing. Instances of patients being turned away from 
overburdened hospitals due to lack of vacant beds became the new normal. The scenario of 
patients holding oxygen cylinder rushing from pillar to post in search of bed in AIIMS Patna is a 
testimony to fact that tear apart humanity. The Committee is aggrieved at the poor state of 
healthcare system and therefore, recommends the Government to increase the investment in 
public health and take appropriate steps to decentralize the healthcare services/fac ilities in the 
country. 
                             (Para 2.34) 
 

5 
 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.15 The Committee is pained to observe that in RML hospital out of the 1572 beds, only 242 
beds were dedicated COVID beds whereas in Safdarjung Hospital, out of 2 873 beds, only 289 
were reserved for Covid patients. The Committee fails to understand the rationale behind the 
miniscule number of beds reserved for Covid patients in the Central Government Hospitals 
especially at a time when the number of Covid patients was increasing rapidly in the capital city. 
The Committee, therefore, desires the Ministry to submit a note on the rationale for allocating 
such limited number of beds for COVID patients. The Committee would like to be apprised 
regarding the status of beds  exclusively reserved for COVID patients in the capital of the 
country. 
                             (Para 2.35) 
Action Taken 
1.16 Recommendation of the Committee to increase the investment in public health system is 
acknowledged and agreed upon. In this regard, it is submitted that under National Health 
Mission, support is provided to the States/UTs to strengthen their public healthcare system duly 
adopting a health system approach and as NHM targets to build a network for public health 
facilities with He alth & Wellness Centres at the grassroot level and District Hospitals, with 
robust referral linkage, to offer Comprehensive primary and secondary care services to citizens at 
the District level. For e.g., the increase in the number of public health facilit ies from 2005 to 
2020 is as below; 
o With respect to Sub Health Centres, from 1,46,026 to 1,57,411; w.r.t Primary Health 
Centres, from 23,236 to 24,855; w.r.t Community Health Centres, from 3,346 to 5,335; 
w.r.t District hospitals, from 635 to 756; W.r.t Fir st Referral Units, from 940 to 3,122; 
w.r.t 24x7 Delivery Points, from 2,243 to 15,494. Thus, implementation of NHM has not 
only contributed to increase in the institutional capacities for service delivery but also has 
led to development of capacities for targeted interventions of the various National 
Programmes under the NHM. 
o Further, Under Ayushman Bharat, flagship initiative, it is envisaged to establish 1.5 lakhs 
Health and Wellness Centres by transforming Sub Health Centres and Primary Health 
Centres a cross the country to provide comprehensive primary healthcare closer to the 
people with the focus on preventive and promotive healthcare. 
1.17 Also, under COVID19 India Package support, States/UTs were financially supported and 
all the States/UTs are reque sted that a comprehensive plan may be prepared and steps may be 
taken for augmentation in bed capacities wherever necessary through identification of additional 
hospitals, preparation of field hospital facilities, ensuring sufficient oxygen supported beds,  
oxygen supplies, ICU beds and deployment of requisite HR, training & mentoring of doctors and 
nurses for management of patients, strengthen ambulance services & centralized call centre -
based services for allocation of beds to augment their bed capacities. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.18 The Committee agrees with the Department that the pandemic has led to an 
unprecedented increase in the demand of non-invasive Oxygen Cylinders and instances of lack of 

6 
 
Oxygen Cylinders in the hospitals had also been reporte d. The Committee, therefore, strongly 
advocates National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority to take appropriate measures for capping 
the price of the Oxygen Cylinders so that the availability as well as affordability of the Oxygen 
Cylinders is ensured in all  hospitals for medical consumption. The Committee also recommends 
the Government for encouraging adequate production of Oxygen for ensuring its supply as per 
demand in the hospitals.     
                                                                                                                                       (Para 2.38)  
Action Taken 
1.19 With regard to capping the price of Medical Oxygen, MoHFW vide letter no. Z -
3014/45/2020-RCH dated 15th September 2020 and letter no. Z -33O14/ 45/ 2020-RCH/Pt. File-
3 dated 23rd September 2020 has communicated to Department of Pharmaceuticals and National 
Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) to take all necessary steps to regulate the availability 
& pricing of Liquid Medical Oxygen (LMO) & Medical Oxygen cylinders. 
 In order to encourage adequate production of oxygen for ensuring its supply as per demand: 
o Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is closely monitoring the availability and supply 
of Medical Oxygen and necessary infrastructure available with respecti ve State/UT for 
management of COVID-19 effectively.  
o 1,02,400 oxygen cylinders were procured in April and May of 2020 and distributed to 
states to enable easier access of medical oxygen to end users. Further orders for oxygen 
cylinders have been placed for  additional 1,27,000 cylinders including 54,000 jumbo 
cylinders (D type) as well as 73,000 regular cylinders (B type).  
o Union Health Ministry vide order dated 18.04.2021 has restricted industrial use of 
oxygen. As per the said order, as amended by a furthe r order dated 21.04.2021, supply of 
oxygen to all industrial use was prohibited with effect from 22.04.2021 except for certain 
specified industries.  
o Railways is being used for long distance transport of tankers through Roll on – Roll Off 
(RORO) service. A ir transport of empty tankers to cut the Turn Around Time has also 
been initiated to deal with the emergencies.  
o Defence Ministry is coordinating with oxygen suppliers for air-lifting of tankers.  
o All the States have been advised rational use of oxygen and to prohibit the wasteful usage 
by strict monitoring.  
o States are also advised to undertake oxygen consumption audit in hospitals including 
private hospitals and to undertake facility -wise/hospital-wise oxygen inventory mapping 
and advance planning for timely replenishment so that there is no stock out. 
o Union Health Ministry is in the process of commissioning of 162 PSA plants (154 MT 
capacity) across the country.  
o Further, 500 more PSA plants are planned to be installed in the hospitals in district 
headquarters to enhance oxygen generation in smaller cities and towns.  

7 
 
1.20 Indigenous technology for PSA plants developed by DRDO (individual plant capacity of 
1000 litre/min) and CSIR (individual plant capacity of 500 litre/min) is being explored for ramp -
up of PSA plant availability.   
Observation/Recommendation 
1.21 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry for augmenting the testing 
infrastructure in such a short period of time and believes that testing isolating and treating holds 
the key for containing the virus. 
                             (Para 2.40) 
Action Taken 
1.22     Observation of the Hon‟ble Committee have been taken note of. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.23 The Committee, in its 117th Report on the Allied and Healthcare Professions Bill 2018, 
has exhaustively examined the different clauses of the Bill. The Committee had recommended for 
need of de -medicalisation and bringing forth the Allied and Healthcare Profession to the 
forefront of patient care and safety. With the unprecedented testing times of the current 
pandemic where the health sector world over is struggling with heavy disease burden the allied 
health sector needs to be strengthened. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry that 
along with medical professionals, the  quality management of nursing and allied professionals in 
the country must also be ensured. 
                             (Para 2.67) 
Action Taken 
1.24 Based on the recommendations of the Committee's 117 thReport on the Allied and 
Healthcare Professions Bill 2018, a revised Bill namely the National Commission for Allied and 
Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) Bill, 2020 was prepared and introduced and passed by 
Parliament on 24 th March 2021. The Bill is for maintaining standards of education and practice 
through the constitution of National Commission and corresponding State Councils for Allied 
and Healthcare Professions for more than 50 allied and healthcare professions. 
 For improving the quality of Nursing Services in the country the following steps are being 
taken: 
o In tune with the reforms in medical education sector and Allied Healthcare professionals‟ 
sector, Nursing Education Regulation is also being reformed. A National Nursing and 
Midwifery Commission (NNMC) Bill, 2020 has been drafted by an Expert Committe e 
and Public comments on the Bill have been obtained. The draft Bill proposes to create a 
new institutional framework, in the form of a National Nursing and Midwifery 
Commission and four Autonomous Boards for regulating all aspects relating to education, 
training and services of nursing and midwifery personnel. The draft Bill is under 
examination in the Ministry. 

8 
 
o A Central Sector Scheme called „Development of Nursing Services‟ is being 
implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare which focuses o n the in -
service training of nurses in the field of specialization; infrastructure development by way 
of up -gradation of schools of nursing to colleges of nursing, thereby increasing the 
availability of graduate nurses.  
o Nurse Practitioners Course in Criti cal Care at M.Sc. (N) level has been started and State 
governments are being requested to create such posts in govt. and private hospitals. 
o To ensure that in-service nursing personnel continue to update their technical knowledge 
and clinical skills in the ever-evolving health sector, renewal of license of nursing 
personnel, once every five years, has been linked with 150 hours of Continuing Nursing 
Education. 
1.25 Realizing the need of de -medicalization, both the NCAHP Bill and the proposed NNMC 
Bill provide for strengthening of nursing, allied and healthcare professionals and defining scope 
of practice of nursing / allied healthcare personnel and for task shifting. Task shifting refers to 
moving specific tasks to specialized nursing and allied & healt hcare professionals for better 
reorganization of health workforce and improved healthcare. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.26 The Committee notes the Ministry's initiative to ensure appropriate risk communication 
through SMS and caller tunes. However, the Com mittee feels that information dissemination 
regarding covid-19 in rural areas is still inadequate. The Committee, therefore, recommends the 
Ministry to encourage active participation of self -help groups, the Panchayats and the Gram 
Sabhas for better public health messaging. The Committee also recommends the Ministry to take 
more inclusive measures for bringing a behavioral change regarding handwashing and mask 
wearing among the masses. 
                             (Para 2.76) 
Action Taken 
1.27 To brace up for the Covid -19 pandemic, the Ministry of Health & FW took several 
measures so that the campaigns on do‟s and don‟ts and Covid Appropriate Behaviours (CAB) 
were amplified up to the last mile, on a real time basis.   For this purpose, the Minist ry wrote to 
17 Central line Ministries, State Governments,  and also engaged directly with Development 
Partners to activate their field level networks to reach out to Self Help Groups, Panchayats and 
Gram Sabhas. The Ministry‟s own network of ASHAs and ANMs  was also activated to carry 
messages on CAB to the last mile.   This was over and above consistent messaging through 
mobile caller tunes, Community Radio Stations, LokSabha TV, DD News Channel and lastly 
through the Jan Andolan launched by the Hon‟ble PM on October 8, 2020. 
MANAGING MEDICAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.28 The Committee takes note of the different initiatives taken by ICMR for devising 
treatment protocol for Covid-19. However, the Committee observes that in the initial phase there 
was certain ambiguity in the treatment protocol for Covid -19 which is somehow attributed to the 
mutating strain of Corona virus. The Committee understands that devising a full proof treatment 
plan will have to be substantiated by different p hases of clinical trials and have to be governed 

9 
 
by strict protocols. The Committee, therefore, recommends ICMR to widen the scope of its 
clinical research and studies and keep on updating its database which could prove beneficial in 
containing and mitigat ing Covid -19 as well as such future outbreaks. The Committee also 
recommends ICMR to collaborate with other international institutes and pharmaceutical 
companies to test the safety and effectiveness of different drugs and devices. 
                             (Para 3.5) 
Action Taken 
1.29 The COVID-19 Clinical Management Protocol was prepared by MoHFW in consultation 
with AIIMS, New Delhi; National Task Force under ICMR and the Joint Monitoring Group 
under Directorate General of Heal th Services. Last updated algorithm for clinical management 
protocol was issued on 23.04.2021. Similarly, a protocol for Management of Covid - 19 in the 
pediatric Age Group was issued by MoHFW on 29.04.2021. 
 ICMR conducted the world‟s largest clinical tria l on benefit of using plasma therapy in 
COVID-19 infected patients (PLACID Trial). The trial indicated no significant benefit of 
plasma therapy. Thereafter ICMR has issued an advisory in November 2020 regarding use of 
convalescent plasma in COVID-19 infected patients. 
 ICMR has collaborated with Biological Evans to evaluate the efficacy of the hyper -immune 
horse serum for treating COVID -19 infected patients. Similar studies are underway for 
similar product of Serum Institute of India. 
 Collaborations with man ufacturers like ZydusCadila for evaluating monoclonal antibodies 
for treating COVID-19 are also underway. 
 International partnerships were undertaken in the form of WHO Solidarity Trial. Other 
International collaborations are also underway. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.30 The Committee is of the view that only those drugs whose efficacy for treating COVID -19 
patients have been established should be used for hospitalized patients and the drugs should be 
prescribed only after multicentric trials and detailed study. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends the Ministry to issue clear guidelines for safe use of drugs. The Committee notes 
that there have been instances where certain drugs were prescribed for COVID -19, but clinical 
trials gave unfavorable results. The  Committee, in this connection, strongly recommends the 
Ministry to issue strict guidelines against use of such drugs when the evidence conclusively 
shows that it does not work for Covid treatment. The Committee believes that only drugs with 
reliable data and research should be used among Covid patients, especially for patients with co -
morbidities. 
                             (Para 3.14) 
Action Taken 
1.31 The National Task Force co -chaired by Member (Health) NITI Aayog and DG, ICMR 
and the Joint Monitoring Group under DGHS recommends the drugs for clinical management of 
COVID-19 cases that gets documented in National COVID-19 Clinical Management Protocol.  

10 
 
 National COVID -19 Clinical Management Protocol clearly describes the evidence -based 
drugs to be used routinely and a set of investigational drugs to be used only in a defined sub -
group of patients under close medical supervision. 
 This protocol continues to  be revised from time to time based on emerging scientific 
evidence on therapeutics. 
1.32 The protocol has been widely disseminated and made available on the website of 
Ministry. It has also been discussed in technical sessions organized by Centers of Excellence at 
National and State levels, webinars, etc. 
Observation/Recommendation

strategy but subsequently the whole population should be vaccinated. The Committee also 
recommends the Ministry to upgrade its cold -chain storage system so that country wide

Observation/Recommendation 
1.36 The Committee is of the view that letting people  get infected with the virus till they 
develop herd immunity would result in a high mortality rate. The Committee agrees that given 
the poor health infrastructure in the country, the effect could be adverse. The Committee notes 
that the trials of the vacci nes are still underway and providing vaccine dose to a population of 
1.3 billion will take time. The Committee, therefore, believes the best strategy available at 
present is to increase the testing capacity and isolate the affected persons to contain the f urther 
spread of the virus and keep infected persons under appropriate medical observation. 
                          (Para 3.33) 
Action Taken 
1.37 Noted. The Government of India is following the same guidance. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.38 The Committee is of the view that the pandemic Covid -19 has highlighted the need for 
creation of a robust network of laboratories in the country. The Committee observes that though 
in the beginning only ICMR -National Institute of Virology (NIV) was tasked with the initial 
testing of suspected cases but in a short span of time, testing capacity was escalated and other 
viral research and diagnostic laboratories were commissioned. Even then identification of only 
13 VRDLs across 11 states in a country with 1.3  billion population is indicative of the fact that 
the testing capacity was highly inadequate. It is quite disheartening to note that many States did 
not have the required infrastructure for testing facilities. This led to overburdening of the labs 
and cau sed inordinate delays in giving the test results. The Committee is, therefore, of the 
considered view that the laboratory infrastructure in the country needs to be strengthened along 
with the technical workforce required to operate these labs. 
                             (Para 3.44) 
Action Taken 
1.39 Continuous augmentation of COVID -19 testing infrastructure is ongoing. As on date 
(12/5/2020), India has 2535 molecular testing labs. Testing facilities for Rapid Antigen Test are 
available in all 741 districts of the country. A new centrally sponsored sch eme, PM Atma  
Nirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana , will be launched with an outlay of about Rs. 64,180 crores 
over 6 years. This will develop capacities of primary, secondary, and tertiary care Health 
Systems, strengthen existing national institutions, and create new institutions, to cater to 
detection and cure of new and emerging diseases. This will be in addition to the National Health 
Mission. The initiative includes support for: 

12 
 
(i) strengthening of the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), its 5 regional 
branches and 20 metropolitan health surveillance units; and  
(ii) setting up of 9 Bio -Safety Level III laboratories and 4 regional National Institutes for 
Virology. 
(iii) setting up integrated public health labs in all districts and 3382 block public health units 
in 11 states, 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.40 The Committee is of the view that a differentiated approach with aggressive testing in 
containment zones and cities with high level of infection could have arrested the spread of 
infection. However, with unlocking, the infection has now spread to different parts of the 
country. The Committee also believes that Tracing, Tracking, Testing, Treating and Technology 
(5Ts) are the answer to tackling Covid-19 and the Ministry has been working on all the fronts. 
However, the Committee still feels that the coordination between the Centre and the States needs 
further strengthening for better result. The required infrastructure to imbibe the 5Ts c annot be 
established overnight rather it demands adequate financial aid and specialized human resources. 
                             (Para 3.46) 
Action Taken 
1.41 Coordination between Central and State Governments is ensured through regular VC 
meetings at the level of Hon‟ble PM, Hon‟ble HFM, Cabinet Secretary and senior officials from 
MoHFW. A Committee of Secretaries under Cabinet Secretary is reviewing the situation 
regularly. He has also held regular video conferences with States/UTs. Hon‟ble Union Hea lth 
Minister and Senior officers in the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare are constantly 
reviewing the evolving scenario and have held 106 video conferences so far with State Health 
functionaries. 
1.42 On matters related to lockdown, community wide quara ntine, MHA is also coordinating 
with their respective State Disaster Management Authorities. States are being provided with 
requisite guidance under DM Act by MHA.

of AS/JS) for all States/UTs to constantly interact with States and act as a bridge between Center 
and State. 
1.44 Technical guidance is facilitated by MoHFW. MoHFW has also established a Facilitation 
Center (011 -23060777) wherein States are provided information on hospital infrastructure 
augmentation, therapeutics, diagnostics, vaccines, guidance documents etc. In addition, Central 
multi-disciplinary teams are being deployed. So far a total of 155 teams have been deployed to 
various States/UTs. 
1.45 The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme has field outreach through its District 
and State units. Central IDSP coordinates with the State and District units on regular basis at the 
operational level.  ICMR has been closely working with the centre and s tates to devise the most 
effective and feasible methods for testing in containment and non -containment zones. 
Laboratories have been established in difficult terrains and far -flung areas like Ladakh, Sikkim, 

13 
 
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland as well as other Nor th Eastern states, Lakshadweep and Andaman 
&Nicobar island. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.46 The Committee was given to understand that various diagnostic kits being used in 
carrying out Covid -19 Testing, include kits imported from other countries. The Comm ittee is of 
the view that with an enabling policy framework, the Indian medical device industry could grow 
by leaps and bounds. The Committee strongly advocates providing support to the indigenous 
medical device manufacturing industry to make India self -sufficient and promote local 
production under PM‟s flagship programme of AtmaNirbhar Bharat - that focuses on self -
reliance and local production. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to formulate 
specific schemes for providing financial incentive s as well as infrastructure assistance to the 
industry that would work like „Sanjeevanibooti‟ to already slackening economy growth. The 
Ministry should devise segment specific approach for consumables, implants, diagnostic imaging 
and kits and other medical devices to boost up healthcare industry. 
                             (Para 3.48) 
Action Taken

indigenous manufacturers.

Observation/Recommendation

made in the 119th Report that the budgetary allocation to Department of Health Research should

COVID Management under Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY Scheme 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.52 The Committee is equally appreh ensive about the ground realities. Covid testing and 
treatment may not be available in all public hospitals. Given the fragile network of our public 
hospitals that struggled to deal with the increasing cases of Corona, instances of private 
hospitals chargi ng exorbitant medical fees for Covid treatment are being reported. In such a 
scenario, where only the affluent could afford treatment, the Committee feels that free Covid 
treatment under PMJAY could provide a sigh of relief to the entitled beneficiaries an d the 
economically weaker sections of the society. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry 
to constantly make efforts to minimise the out of pocket expenditure of patients due to Covid and 
update the details of the beneficiaries on the scheme's IT System. 
                           (Para   4.13) 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.53 The Committee also appreciates the helpline services offered by NHA, however, outreach 
of these services in the rural areas needs to be ensured. The Committee, therefore, recommends 
the Ministry to create adequate awareness of these services in the rural areas as well. 
                             (Para 4.16) 
Action Taken

beneficiaries about their entitlements under the scheme is being implemented. Due to COVID 
on-ground activities have been affected, however, other media vehicles such as print media, 
radio campaign, telecast of beneficiary testimonials via Doordarshan, mass messaging th rough 
SMS etc. are being implemented. Outreach programme like school contact program, activation 
programs at village level, van campaigns etc. are planned to be undertaken suitably in

PMJAY helpline with State helplines to ensure that patient does not face difficulty at the time of 
emergency. 
 

15

authorized under the scheme. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.56 The Committee would like the Ministry to ensure that the benefits of the Pradhan Mantri 
Garib Kalyan Yojana actually reach to, healthcare providers, including community health 
workers, fighting COVID-19. The Ministry should also assess the implementation o f the Scheme 
at the ground level.  
                             (Para 4.17) 
Action Taken

Governments and Insurance Company. So far, 208 claims have been processed under the 
scheme. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.58 The Committee understands the crucial situation arising due to pandemic Covid -19 and 
the resultant challenges being faced  with respect to the health infrastructure as well as services. 
Since all the resources stand diverted towards tackling the pandemic, people have been facing 
problems in availing treatment for Covid as well as non -Covid illness. The Committee believes 
that people may not be aware about the grievance redressal system and ways and means of 
registering their complaints. The Committee, however, feels that monitoring of empanelled 
hospitals must be done to ensure that treatment is not denied to anyone because it  will have a 
direct impact on the out of pocket expenditure of the poor patients. The Committee believes that 
it is the moral duty of the Government to take care of its poor citizens especially in critical times 
like these. The Committee recommends to the Ministry as well as NHA that all empanelled 
hospitals must be monitored, fresh directions issued and those found guilty be penalised for 
denying treatment to anyone. 
                             (Para 4.26) 
Action Taken 
1.59 Under the grievance redressal mechanism of scheme, grievances can be lodged on the 
portal, through national call centre 14555 or through mail, letter, fax etc. which are 
acknowledged, recorded, escalated & resolved as per well -defined process. For any comp laint 
regarding denial of treatment by an empanelled hospital, Turn Around Time of 6 hours has been 
defined to resolve the complaint. Such complaints are immediately assigned to respective State 
Grievance Nodal Officer designated at each State Health Agency for necessary action. . Also, the 

16 
 
transaction data generated in empanelled hospitals is monitored on a real -time basis through 
advanced analytics and interactive dynamic dashboards. Based on the monitoring, utilization 
data is analysed for over utilizati on based on different triggers and the results are shared with 
State agencies in real time. Regular joint medical audits are conducted by National Anti -Fraud 
Unit along with State Anti-Fraud Units to identify any wrongdoing. A total of 196 hospitals have 
been de -empanelled as a result of audits undertaken by NAFU and SAFU and total penalties 
worth approximately Rs. 16.55 Crores were levied on the errant entities. 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.60 The Committee is quite apprehensive that lack of awareness especially in the rural areas 
may be major reason for ignorance about healthcare benefits under the AB -PMJAY Scheme. As 
a result of such ignorance many entitled beneficiaries still remain outside t he ambit of the 
Scheme. The Committee, therefore, recommends, especially in the remotest and rural areas, to 
utilise the existing community healthcare workforce, community leaders, gram panchayat etc in 
disseminating information about the Scheme. Periodic awareness campaign about the rights of 
the beneficiaries should be conducted.  
1.61 The Ministry needs to make special efforts and sensitize the entitled beneficiaries so that 
instances of patients paying additional amount in case of any additional medical  procedure are 
avoided. 
                             (Para 4.28) 
Action Taken

Covid Management through AYUSH System 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.72 The Committee opines that the pandemic COVID -19 has highlighted the need for 
mainstreaming Indian system of medicine and employing the alternative and traditional 
medicinal systems. The Committee would like the Government to weigh the relative contributi on 
of both system i.e. system of modern medicine & science and the AYUSH, as complementary to 
each other in the management of diseases. The New Education Policy, 2020 also calls for 
integration of Allopathy with AYUSH Systems of Medicine. The NEP, 2020 exh orts much greater 
emphasis on preventive healthcare and community medicine in all forms of healthcare 
education. The Committee believes that the integration of Indian system with Allopathy would 
not only give medical students better understanding of preven tive healthcare and community 
medicine, as envisioned under NEP, 2020, but at the same time would help the AYUSH 
practitioners to equip themselves to dispense basic medical care at the primary healthcare level. 
The integration of AYUSH with Allopathy is a positive move that would help India move towards 
meeting the goal of universal healthcare by improving access and delivery in remote areas.  
1.73 The Committee, therefore, recommends the Government to make all out efforts for the 
integration of Allopathy with Indian traditional system of medicine.

Management of Post-COVID Complications 
Observation/Recommendation 
1.141 The Committee understands that having defeated the virus is just the beginning of an 
unresearched path of recovery for survivors of severe COVID-19 disease, since COVID 19 is a 
new disease. The post -acute phase of SARS -CoV-2 infection depends on the severity of virus 
attack on different patients. Apart from the fear of unknown, the survivors of COVID 19 venture 
into an unchartered territory o f post COVID complications. Not only do they have to deal with 
fatigue, breathlessness and other physical effects of the disease, but also grapple with the 
psychological impact of it. The Committee is relieved to note that the Government has taken 
cognizance of complexities caused by COVID during post recovery phase and identified 
potential post-acute care needs of recovered COVID -19 patients. The Committee notes that the 
Ministry has adopted integrated holistic approach for managing patients who have recov ered 
from COVID and advised to take care at home. The Committee in this regard recommends the 
Government to put in place healthcare services to ensure a holistic follow -up of post COVID 
treatment of the patients who are showing post COVID complications. It  is also necessary to 
address the possibility of SARS -CoV- 2re-infection, the proportion of adverse reactions after 
hospital discharge and the possible development of other viral and/or bacterial infections. 
                               (Para 6.5)

Observation/Recommendation 
1.180 The Committee reiterates its  considered view that the healthcare spending in India is 
abysmally low for an emerging economy with a population of 1.3 billion. Lack of desired level of 
investment in the health infrastructure has so far resulted into fragility of Indian health 
ecosystem which posed a big hurdle in generating an effective response against the pandemic. 
The Committee has time and again recommended the Ministry for increasing its spending in the 
health sector for ensuring better health infrastructure and health services to the needy common 
masses. The Committee expresses its serious displeasure over the Government's reluctance to act 
upon the Committee's recommendations in letter and spirit. The Committee is assured that the 
serious impact of the pandemic could have been min imized had the Government over the years 
increased its investment in the healthcare system. The Committee is pained to note the trauma 
and distress the public had to undergo due to absence of a dedicated healthcare system. The 
Committee, therefore, strongl y recommends the Government to increase its investments in the 
public healthcare system and make consistent efforts to achieve the National Health Policy 
targets of expenditure up to 2.5% of GDP within two years as the set timeframe of year 2025 is 
far away and the public health cannot be jeopardized till that time schedule.

country‟s health policy with the purpose of strengthening the health sector, and thus necessitates 
a higher investment in creating permanent basic health infrastructure. The Committee also 
believes that a higher budgetary allocation will also boost the healthcare industry and shift the 
focus to Indi an manufacturers and domestic supply chain of products. The Committee believes 
that it is the opportune time to boost India‟s healthcare infrastructure and push for greater 
technology deepening in the healthcare sector.

1.183 Ayushman Bharat, a flagship scheme of Government of India, has been launched to 
achieve the vision of Universal Health Coverage (UHC). This initiative has been designed to 
meet Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and its underlining commitment, which is to 
"leave no one behind." This scheme aims to undertake interventions to holistically address the 
healthcare system (covering prevention, promotion and ambulatory care) at the primary, 
secondary and tertiary level. Ayus hman Bharat adopts a continuum of care approach, 
comprising of two inter-related components, which are - 
 Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) 
 Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) 
1.184 Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) component envisages creation of 1 ,50,000 Health 
and Wellness Centres (HWCs) to deliver Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) bringing 
healthcare closer to the homes of people to deliver an expanded range of services to address the 
primary health care needs of the entire population in t heir area, expanding access, universality 
and equity close to the community. 
1.185 Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya  Yojana (PM-JAY)Ayushman Bharat PM -JAY is the largest 
health assurance scheme in the world which aims at providing a health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per  
family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 10.74 crores poor and 
vulnerable families (approximately 50 crore beneficiaries) that form the bottom 40% of the 
Indian population. Since its launch in September 2018, as on 14 th April, 2021, 1,81,33,191 
hospital admission have taken place.  
1.186 In a bid to further improve public health funding, a new centrally sponsored scheme, PM 
Atma Nirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana, has been announced with an outlay of about Rs. 64,180 
crores over 6 years. This will develop capacities of primary, secondary, and tertiary care Health 
Systems, strengthen existing national institutions, and create new institutions, to cater to 
detection and cure of new and emerging diseases. The main interventions under the scheme are: 
i. Support for 17,788 rural and 11,024 urban Health and Wellness Centers 
ii. Setting up integrated public health labs in all districts and 3382 block public health units 
in 11 states; 
iii. Establishing critical care hospital blocks in 602 districts and 12 central institutions; 
iv. Strengthening of the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), its 5 regional 
branches and 20 metropolitan health surveillance units; 
v. Expansion of the Integrated Health Information Portal to all States/UTs to connect all 
public health labs; 
vi. Operationalisation of 17 new Public Health Units and strengthening of 33 existing Public 
Health Units at Points of Entry, that is at 32 Airports, 11 Seaports and 7 land crossings; 
vii. Setting up of 15 Health Emergency Operation Centers and 2 mobile hospitals; and 

43 
 
viii. Setting up of a national institution for One Health, a Regional Research Platform for 
WHO South East Asia Region, 9 Bio -Safety Level III laboratories and 4 regional 
National Institutes for Virology.

Further Recommendation 
3.5 In view of the loss of life during the second wave of the Covid -19 pandemic, the 
Committee believes that the measures taken by the Ministry to contain/prevent spread of 
SARS-COV-2 proved to be squarely inadequate. The Committee believes that focus should 
be on strengthening of health infrastructure, ensuring adequate availability of beds, 
adequate supply of oxygen cylinders and essential medicines etc . Besides, the G overnment 
must aggressively keep pushing the vaccination program me in terms of granting approval 
to more vaccines, ramping up vaccines’ production, enhancing delivery capacity and 
increasing the vaccination rate.  
 
3.6 With the incidence of highly mutated Omicron (B.1.1.529) strain of Covid virus, the

addressed. The Committee apprehends that rise in mutations in the virus may lead to reporting 
of more virulent and transmissi ble strain of C ovid virus  in the country . The Committee,

closely track Covid cases across the country.

Observation/Recommendation 
3.7 The Committee observes that only 33, 330 and 8,64,517 tests were conducted in the 
month of March and April respectively which increased to 33,878,288 in the month of October. 
The Committee believes that poor contact tracing a nd less testing could have been a factor for 
the exponential growth of COVID cases in the country. The Committee is also worried at the use 

61 
 
of less reliable diagnostic tests which increase the chances of false negatives. Though the Rapid 
Antigen Tests may give faster results but are less reliable than the gold standard RT -PCR tests. 
Large scale use of such tests with low specificity and sensitivity may end up giving false 
negatives and subsequently derail the Covid -19 containment strategy. The Committee is of the 
view that the Government must assess the veracity of Rapid Antigen Test vis -à-vis RT-PCR and 
other diagnostic tests conducted to bring forth the true picture of the testing capacity in the 
country.  
3.8 The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends the Ministry to ramp up the testing 
facilities in the country for more accurate tests. The Committee strongly recommends the testing 
rate through the more reliable RT-PCR tests.

pained to note that although the second wave came almost six months after the peak of the

3.46 The Committee  expresses its concern over prevailing disparities in health

health infrastructure. This is evident from the fact that unlike first wave (peaked is 
September 2020) of the Covid -19 pandemic which largely was restricted to urban areas, 
where testing was introduced rapidly, the second wave  (peaked in May)  largely spread 
through rural towns and villages. The Committee, therefore,  observes that there is dire 
need for improving the  geographical spread of testing facilities in the rural regions of the 
country. The Committee also recommends establishing sync between the PHCs/CHCs with 
the VRDLs in the states.

and more than 4 lakh infected persons have died of Covid -19, therefore, inadequate testing

recommends t hat the Ministry and authority c oncerned must plan testing a s one -step

3.60 The Committee expresses concern over inadequate investment on public health research 
even though innovation play pivotal role in controlling the sp read of disease. The country lacks 
resilient field surveillance to detect potential cluster of diseases. Lack of investment leads to 
dependence on imports of diagnostic kits and development of vaccine and drugs which ultimately 
enhances 'out of pocket expe nditure' of common populace. The Committee strongly recommends 
the higher investment on research and development and innovation in the field of health research 
at multiple levels to contain zoonotic virals like COVID -19 and to establish One Health 
Surveillance System with potential warning system of microbial spill over. The Committee is 
distressed to note the recent UIS data (UNESCO Institute of Statistics data) expressing that India 
invests only 0.65 percent of GDP on Research and Development. India's GER D as a percentage 
of GDP was 0.67 in 2017 and 0.65 in 2018. The Gross domestic expenditure on R&D (GERD) as 
a percentage of GDP is the total intramural expenditure on R&D performed in the national 
territory during a specific reference period expressed as a  percentage of GDP of the national 
territory. The Committee notes that India's GERD is well below the world average and the 
GERD of other countries. Countries like United States of America spend almost 2.84 percent of 
its GDP on research whereas China also  spends 2.19 percent of its GDP on research. The 
Committee deprecates the fact that India's lower appropriation on Research speaks volumes of 
how neglected the R&D sector has been in the country. The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends that the Minis try should at least increase its spending on research to the world 
average of 1.72 as a percentage of GDP within two years. The Committee also recommends the 
Ministry to set specific expenditure targets for R&D and for promotion of science, technology 
and innovation (STI). This dedicated separate budgetary allocation should be supported even in 
financial crisis situations so that research activities do not suffer in the wake of any unforeseen 
circumstances.

COVID Management under Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY Scheme 
Observation/Recommendation 
3.66 The Committee notes that NHA has introduced a process of temporary empanelment for

 All eligible public hospitals including those under the administrative jurisdiction of

 A roadmap is being prepared for empaneling majority 100 bed hospitals under the 
scheme. 
 Prominent corporate hospital chains are being approached for empanelment under the

empaneled hospitals .

Observation/Recommendation 
3.114 The Committee appreciates the pharmacovigilance initiative taken by the Ministry with 
the aim to prevent the adverse drug reaction and safeguard the public health. This is a positive 
step to showcase that Indian traditional system of medicine is not only safe but also scientifically 
validated. The Committee, however, cautions that the fake claims and misleadi ng advertisements 
about ASU&H drugs would not only damage the credibility of AYUSH medicines but also create 
distrust amongst the users of ASU&H drugs as well. The Committee, therefore, recommends the 
Ministry to evolve stringent regulatory framework to ta ckle the problems of failed samples and 
ensure quality control of AYUSH drugs. Strict and exemplary action in a time bound manner 
must be taken against the manufacturers involved in manufacturing of spurious/low quality 
AYUSH drugs. The Ministry ought to f ix the responsibility of the officials concerned who 
approve low/substandard quality drugs. The Ministry must sensitize physicians, pharmacists, 
patients, the pharmaceutical industry and other stakeholders towards reporting adverse drug 
reactions. The Mini stry should also make efforts to strengthen State Government ASU&H 
Pharmacies and drug testing laboratories in tackling the menace of misleading advertisement 
and low quality AYUSH drugs. 
                            (Para 5.23) 
Action Taken 
 
3.115 Ministry of AYUSH has implemented the Central Sector Scheme of Pharmacovigilance 
Program of ASU & H drug since December 2017. Through this scheme a three tier network 
consisting of National Pharmacovigilance Co -ordination Centre (NPvCC), five Intermediary 
PharmacovigilanceCentres (IPvCs) and seventy four Peripheral PharmacovigilanceCentres 
(PPvCs) has been established for safety monitoring of Ayush drugs, reporting of adverse drug 
events and surveillance & reporting of misleading advertisements.   Functionality of the 
pharmacovigilance centres is reviewed periodically. As a result of effective implementation of 
the scheme, pharmacovigilance  centres have reported 9369 misleading advertisements, 185 
COVID -19 related claims and 543 cases of suspected adverse drug reactions of AYUSH drugs. 
Further Recommendation 
3.116 The Committee recommends to evolve stringent regulatory framework to tackle the 
problems of failed samples and ensure quality control of AYUSH drugs. Strict and 
exemplary action in a time bound manner must  be taken against those who are involved in 
manufacturing of spurious/low quality AYUSH drugs. The Committee expects the Ministry 
to fix the responsibility of the officials concerned who approve low/substandard quality 
drugs. The Committee wishes to be informed about the action taken by the responsible 
authorities in dealing with the misleading advertisements and unwarranted claims about 
drugs and other solution s in the last three years. The Committee is of the view that i t is 
high time to effect amendments in the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs and 
Magic Remedies Act 1954 to make the  provisions relating to offences and penalties/

stringent and effective enough to control and contain the misleading advertisements, poor

healthcare services like immunization, maternal, neonatal healthcare facilities, health check-ups, 
screenings etc are not disrupted in the Health and Wellness Centres.  
(Para 4.31) 
Combating the Challenges of Pandemic COVID-19  
Observation/Recommendation 
4.9 The Committee, while considering, the economic consequence of the pandemic on 
women, feels the urgent need for economic emancipation of women by providing them with 
equitable opportunity of employment and enabling their participation in the micro and macro -
decision-making process. In a world, where the share of women in the workforce is already less, 
the Committee believes that financial inequality between men and women will further rise 
sharply. The Committee notes many women are employed in the informal sector which has been 
worst hit due to the pandemic. The Committee therefore recommends the Ministry to make social 
security measures accessible to women and launch specific programmes so that women are able 
to absorb the economic shock and the resultant mental stress caused due to the sudd en job 
losses. 
                             (Para 7.34) 
Action Taken 
4.10 Noted. The matter would be taken up with Ministry of Women and Child Development 
and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.  
Financing the Health Sector 
Observation/Recommendation 
4.11 The Committee also laments the poor state of primary healthcare especially in rural 
areas. The Committee strongly recommends the Ministry to urgently increase its spending under 
the National Rural Health Mission to strengthe n the delivery of health care servicesin the rural 
areas, keeping in view the languishing health infrastructure and inadequate delivery of health 
services to much needed rural population. 
                             (Para 8.11) 
Action Taken 
4.12 The allocation and expenditure by way of releases to the States/UTs under National 
Health Mission shows a positive increasing trend. Further, States/UTs are also instructed to 
increase their State sector health spending to >8% of their budget by 2020.  
4.13 Public health and hospitals being the State subject, besides, the support provided under 
NHM to strengthen the public healthcare delivery system including infrastructure as per 
population norms, States are instructed to desired focus on rural areas and backward areas. 
  

93 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS - AT A GLANCE 
 
ADMINISTRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF LOCKDOWN & UNLOCKING 
 In view of the loss of life during the second wave of the Covid -19 pandemic, the 
Committee believes that the measures taken by the Ministry to contain/prevent spread of 
SARS-COV-2 proved to be squarely inadequate. The Committee believes that focus should 
be on strengthening of health infrastructure, ensuring adequate availability of beds, 
adequate supply of oxygen cylinders and essential medicines etc. Besides, the Government 
must aggressively keep pushing the vaccination programme in terms of granting appr oval 
to more vaccines, ramping up vaccines’ production, enhancing delivery capacity and 
increasing the vaccination rate.  
(Para 3.5) 
 With the incidence of highly mutated Omicron (B.1.1.529) strain of Covid virus, the 
Committee strongly believes that the efficacy of the vaccines must be evaluated. The 
concerns with regards to the new strain developing immunoescape mechanism need to be 
critically addressed. The Committee apprehends that rise in mutations in the virus may 
lead to reporting of more virulent and transmissible strain of Covid virus in the country. 
The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends the Ministry to adopt Zero Toleran ce 
Covid-19 Policy and closely track Covid cases across the country.  
(Para 3.6) 
CONTINGENCY PLAN 
The Committee believes that timely detection and isolation of potentially infectious 
people is very crucial in reducing the impact of the pandemic Covid -19. The importance of 
diagnostic testing therefore, cannot be overlooked. An efficient and widely deployed testing 
mechanism will go a long way in preventing the spread of the infection. The Committee is 
pained to note that although the second wave came almost six months after the peak of the 
first wave, India’s testing infrastructure remained abysmal and highly insufficient. The 
Committee is of the opinion that to combat current pandemic Covid -19 and other future 
emergencies, India must realise its full testing  capacity and augment’s this capacity even 
further. The government should ensure that the testing should far outpace the growth of 
the cases to arrest future waves of Covid-19 early.  
 (Para 3.11) 
 The Committee also notes that with the new strain of Covid, Omicron (B.1.1.529) 
exhibiting 30+ mutations, tracking and testing facilities especially at airports must also be 
strengthened and rigorous testing and screening of travelers must be carried out. The 
Committee also recommends the Ministry to explore imposing travel restrictions and 
isolating passengers from 'at -risk' countries, as part of their new covid strain containment 
strategy. With WHO designating Omicorn as "Variant of Concern", the Governme nt must 
take immediate measures to prevent the transmission of any newer strains in the country.  
(Para 3.12) 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation for creation of the 'Indian Health 
Service' (IHS) in the Center and across States as a dedicated, effi cient, and adequately 

94 
 
resourced public health cadre on the pattern of Indian Administrative Service (IAS). It also 
recommends that the Ministry should issue specific guidelines to the states regarding timely 
payment of wages to the healthcare workers parti cularly who are the foot soldiers of the 
healthcare system. The Committee further strongly advocates for strengthening the 
network of ASHAs, ANMs and other community health workers and the necessary support 
in the healthcare delivery system. The Committee underlines the need to expedite the 
reforms in regulatory mechanism of dental and nursing education.  
(Para 3.20) 
 The Committee is constrained to observe that the recent Second Wave of the Covid -
19 saw unprecedented price escalation and shortage of oxygen  cylinder and other critical 
equipments and drugs. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Governments must 
set up adequate Oxygen manufacturing plants and a robust supply and support mechanism 
for States to ensure uninterrupted supply of oxygen and other medical equipments and 
drugs for use under emergency situation. The Committee is also concerned about the 
exorbitant prices of the critical medicines during pandemics. Given the fact that the 
National Pharmaceutical Pricing  Authority (NPPA) updates t he price caps of such 
medicines and drugs, the Committee, recommends a strict and regular monitoring over 
adherence to this price capping, especially in the event of pandemic like situation.  
(Para 3.26) 
 The Committee believes that Covid -19 pandemic has b rought to the fore the 
importance of bio-medical waste collection, management and its disposal. Now -a-days, the 
management of biomedical waste has become a major concern as bio -medical waste is 
being generated not only from hospitals but also from househol ds. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends, that the capacity of the 200 odd Common Bio -medical Waste 
Treatment Facilities (CBWTF) spread across the nation must be augmented for their 
optimal utilisation. The ULBs (Urban Local Bodies), concerned authorities and other 
stakeholders must be directed to ensure minimal leakages in the waste (bio -medical) 
journey from point of origin to disposal. States need to be sensitized about the guidelines of 
disposal of biomedical waste. For this to happen, proper training a nd awareness 
programmes should be organized at the district and block level to educate both the workers 
of municipalities and the public at large for better bio-medical waste management.  
(Para 3.31) 
 The Committee notes the Government's efforts in combating the Covid-19, however, 
the Committee would like to be apprised of the 'plan of action' with respect to utilization of 
Rs. 64179.55 crores allocated for strengthening of public health infrastructure for 
pandemic preparedness. The Ministry may also apprise the Committee about the feedback 
and assessment pertaining to key performance indicators related to surveillance, testing, 
hospital infrastructure, logistics at the district levels. The Committee obs erves that the 
steps taken to combat the second wave of pandemic were not sufficient and more concrete 
action could have been undertaken to contain the impact of Covid -19. The Committee 
believes that structural and operational corrections are required to p repare for the future 
health emergencies. The Committee, therefore, recommends that every State should 
establish at least one medical college and hospital as 'Centre of Excellence' for proper 
health surveillance during emergency situation.   

95 
 
(Para 3.37) 
MANAGING MEDICAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT 
 The Committee is constrained to observe that vaccine scarcity is the major 
constraint of the Government's "Covid Vaccination" programme. The Committee wishes 
to point out that the Government failed in devising a pla n for the systematic and continual 
availability of the vaccine. The Committee therefore, recommends the Ministry to 
collaborate with all the vaccine manufacturers in the country and ensure that vaccines are 
easily available to the general public to catch pace of vaccination drive in all States/UTs.  
(Para 3.43) 
 The Committee expresses its concern over prevailing disparities in health 
infrastructure including testing facilities in the rural and urban areas despite the efforts 
put in by the Government. The C ommittee hopes that the Government has learnt some 
lessons from the disastrous second wave of the pandemic Covid -19. With the threat of a 
third wave looming around the Government should utilise the time in strengthening the 
public health infrastructure. Th is is evident from the fact that unlike first wave (peaked is 
September 2020) of the Covid -19 pandemic which largely was restricted to urban areas, 
where testing was introduced rapidly, the second wave (peaked in May) largely spread 
through rural towns and villages. The Committee, therefore, obs erves that there is dire 
need for improving the geographical spread of testing facilities in the rural regions of the 
country. The Committee also recommends establishing sync between the PHCs/CHCs with 
the VRDLs in the states.  
(Para 3.46) 
 The Committee is also concerned about the efficacy of the present vaccines and the 
possibility of mutated strain like Omicron evading vaccine immunity. The Committee, 
therefore recommends the Government to conduct more research and examine the need of 
administering booster dose of vaccines for containing the newer strain of virus.   
(Para 3.47) 
 The Committee also recommends Indian SARS -CoV-2 Genomic Consortia 
INSACOG to closely monitor the new strain of the virus and work towards upgrading the 
genome sequencing infrastructure in the country.  
(Para 3.48) 
The Committee strongly believes that pre-emptive testing is key to rein in the spread 
of the pandemic. Extensive testing provides a window to understand the spatial spreading 
pattern of transmissions of the pandemic Covid -19 thus extending research work and 
opportunity to devise remedial plan based on the conclusions drawn from that research 
work. During the second wave new cases surged as high as 4.5 lakhs a day in April, 2021 
and more than 4 lakh infected persons have di ed of Covid-19, therefore, inadequate testing 
does not provide the clear picture of the transmission on the ground. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry and authority concerned must plan testing as one -step 
ahead of virus transmission so that infected people are traced and quarantined early, which 
help in breaking the transmission chain.  
(Para 3.51) 

96 
 
 The Committee observes that the North-East region was engulfed during the second 
wave of the pandemic Covid -19. The Committee’s apprehension came true a s whatever 
efforts authorities took to prevent spread of the pandemic proved inadequate. The 
Committee believes that it's high time Ministry pulls up its socks and takes concrete steps 
to improve the largely insufficient healthcare facilities in the North -East Region of the 
country.  
(Para 3.54) 
 The Ministry should ensure that its guidelines and advisories regarding Covid 
Appropriate Behaviour (CAB) are strictly implemented in letter and spirit.  
(Para 3.55) 
 The Committee recommends that the Government mu st ensure the establishment of 
at least one BSL -3 lab in each VRDL spread across different States of the country. The 
Committee would like to reiterate its recommendation mentioned in the Committee's 127 th 
Report for establishing at least one BSL -4 lab in each zone/ region viz. North, East, West, 
Central and South. The Committee hopes that the Government would ensure fast -track 
establishment of both BSL-3 and BSL-4 labs within a fixed timeline. The Government must 
chalk out counter -strategy to make country bio-secured against the menace of bio 
terrorism.   
(Para 3.59) 
 The Committee notes that even though the budgetary allocation for DHR is 
witnessing a gradual increase, but the enhanced allocation is not commensurate to the 
increased financial implications involved on account of pandemic Covid -19. The 
Committee is of th e firm view that preparedness and prevention of the outbreak of third 
wave of pandemic Covid -19 would require public investment in research work, including 
genome sequencing and zoonotic surveillance. The Committee notes that in terms of the 
percentage of the GDP (Real) (as per first quarter for FY -21) the public expenditure for 
health research is a meagre 0.02%. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its 
recommendation for a substantial increase in spending on research to the world average of 
1.72 as a percentage of GDP within two years.  
(Para 3.62) 
 The Committee acknowledges the Ministry’s efforts in spreading the network of 
Viral Research & Diagnostics Laboratories, Multi - Disciplinary Research Units and Modal 
Rural Health Research Units in the country. I t however strongly believes that 
incorporating modern technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) as positive intervention 
in these initiatives can bear rich dividends in terms of quality, delivery and cost 
optimization of healthcare delivery services. Therefore, the Committee reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministry must increase funding for machine learning and 
artificial intelligence-based projects and encourage the development of AI based systems, 
methods and tools in healthcare.  
(Para 3.65) 
 
 

97 
 
COVID MANAGEMENT UNDER AYUSHMAN BHARAT-PMJAY SCHEME 
 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry in terms of attracting 
investment by private sector in underserved areas. The Committee desires to know 
whether any assessment has been made with r espect to identifying such areas and States 
which need urgent assistance to strengthen their health infrastructure and incorporating 
the targeted beneficiaries within the ambit of the Scheme. The Committee seeks to know 
number of hospitals empanelled in the rural areas out of the 141 empanelled hospitals. The 
Committee recommends that more hospitals having facilities to provide emergency services 
arising out of pandemics like Covid -19 should be empanelled in the rural areas of the 
country.  
(Para 3.70)  
 The Committee fails to comprehend the rationale behind freezing the beneficiary 
database and thus depriving the deserving large chunk of poor people from availing the 
benefits of AB -PMJAY, especially in rural areas. The Committee understands that the 
objective of the scheme can only be fully realized if the poor people who actually need the 
benefits are enrolled in this scheme at the earliest. The Committee strongly recommends 
the NHA (National Health Authority) to expand the beneficiary base under the scheme  in 
consultation with other Ministries/Departments implementing other social security schemes 
in the country.  
(Para 3.73) 
 The Committee firmly believes that quality healthcare facilities in the rural areas 
can be developed by encouraging the participatio n of the private sector in the development 
of healthcare systems. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation for 
engaging both private and public sector for ensuring robust delivery of healthcare services 
under the Scheme Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY). 
(Para 3.76) 
COVID MANAGEMENT THROUGH AYUSH SYSTEM 
 The Committee acknowledges the research work being carried out by various 
organizations under the wings of the Ministry of AYUSH. However, the Committee 
believes tha t more needs to be done to equip the traditional systems of medicine with 
scientific base grounded on in -depth research. The Committee desires that AYUSH 
research work carried out by the institutes aimed towards recording and publishing the 
detailed process of extracting the active ingredient from herbs/plants, its effect initially in 
cell models, then in animals, and finally human trials. To facilitate transition from 
alternative systems to mainstream systems of medicine, it is all the more necessary to bu ild, 
promote and sustain this evidence based framework for the practitioners of the traditional 
systems.  
(Para 3.90) 
The Committee notes the wide range of research studies going on in AYUSH 
research Councils with respect to management of Covid -19, however, the Committee finds 
that the Ministry of AYUSH has not given any justification for delay in approvals for 
clinical and population based research studies. The Committee reiterates its 

98 
 
recommendation seeking clear guidelines with respect to research studie s along with 
proper timelines for the approval process. The Committee would also like to emphasize 
that the outcome of all these research studies especially related to the Covid -19 must be 
recorded, published and adequately placed in the public domain. The  Committee may also 
be apprised of AYUSH research outcomes highlighting concrete evidence in management 
of Covid-19.  
(Para 3.113) 
 The Committee recommends to evolve stringent regulatory framework to tackle the 
problems of failed samples and ensure qualit y control of AYUSH drugs. Strict and 
exemplary action in a time bound manner must be taken against those who are involved in 
manufacturing of spurious/low quality AYUSH drugs. The Committee expects the Ministry 
to fix the responsibility of the officials co ncerned who approve low/substandard quality 
drugs. The Committee wishes to be informed about the action taken by the responsible 
authorities in dealing with the misleading advertisements and unwarranted claims about 
drugs and other solutions in the last th ree years. The Committee is of the view that it is 
high time to effect amendments in the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs and 
Magic Remedies Act 1954 to make the provisions relating to offences and penalties/ 
stringent and effective enough to contro l and contain the misleading advertisements, poor 
quality products, cases of adverse reactions, etc.  
(Para 3.116) 
 The Committee is disappointed to observe that the Ministry of AYUSH is silent on 
its recommendation requiring a dedicated AYUSH Covid Care C entre in all the states. The 
Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry should undertake concrete steps to 
popularize the Indian systems of medicine to complement the modern system of medicine 
in management of Covid -19. The Committee strongly de sires the Ministry to contemplate 
on this and apprises the Committee in this regard.  
(Para 3.119) 
The Committee emphasizes that the major roadblock in delivering the quality 
healthcare services is insufficient public health spending. Needless to say, unless the 
government sets aside sufficient funds for healthcare, the prevailing state of public health  
care systems cannot be improved. Inadequate public spending increases Out of Pocket 
expenditure owing to irrational pricing of life saving equipments, drugs etc, as was evident 
in the second wave of pandemic Covid -19. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
expenditure in healthcare must be enhanced adequately to ensure liquidity and cash flow 
availability. This will help ease out financial distress in healthcare and infrastructure and 
as a result the medium sized hospitals and nursing homes can cont ribute in managing the 
health emergencies.  
(Para 3.123) 
 The Committee further recommends the Government to evolve a mechanism to 
regulate the pricing of life saving drugs, particularly during emergencies and its effective 
implementation.  
(Para 3.124) 

99 
 
 The Committee expects Government to ensure that education facilities for students 
particularly of economically weaker sections do not suffer further due to future Covid -19 
waves. The Committee takes note of growing public debate over re -opening of schools. The 
Committee may be apprised of whether the Ministry has done any studies regarding 
various age-group of students with respect to their immune response, mental health, ability 
to practice social distancing norms and other critical parameters affecting th eir health 
before allowing reopening of schools. The Committee notes that physical and mental health 
of children has been the area of concern during pandemic Covid -19.  The Committee 
maybe apprised of studies carried out on impact of online classes, absenc e of classroom 
schooling on overall development of children.  
(Para 3.127) 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry had projected an amount of Rs. 5435.55 
crore in BE 2021 -22 for promoting various Schemes in AYUSH sector to which the  
Ministry of Finance all ocated an amount of Rs.2970.30 crore for the year 2021 -22 which is 
39.97 per cent more than the allocation made in 2020 -21. The Committee believes that the 
Ministry of AYUSH is capable of absorbing more funds under its different schemes. The 
Committee, therefore recommends that the Ministry of AYUSH should plead for increased 
allocation from the Ministry of Finance in the ensuing financial years.  
(Para 3.131)
